description: The simplest Caro-Kann: White trades early and builds a clean, solid center while Black gets easy development with the bishop out before ...e6. A positional line where understanding piece placement matters more than memorization — ideal for learning the Caro-Kann's solid foundations.

lines.description: After 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5, White releases the tension with 3.exd5 cxd5. Instead of the sharp 4.c4, White develops simply with 4.Bd3 and Black responds 4...Nc6. White supports the center with 5.c3, Black develops 5...Nf6, and after 6.Bf4 Black pins with 6...Bg4. The symmetrical structure means small advantages — better piece placement, the bishop pair, or a timely central break — decide the game.
